render_postal_reproducer_script("records.csv", "postal_code", tempdir()) #> [1] "library(ONgeoR)

# Point this at your own input file.
input_file <- "records.csv"
postal_col <- "postal_code"
output_dir <- "/tmp/RtmpH0raxI"

records <- utils::read.csv(input_file, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)

# resolve_postal() reports codes in the correspondence's own format, so
# the join key has to be normalized on this side too. Joining on the raw
# column silently drops every code that was not already typed as "A1A 1A1".
# resolve_postal() returns a row per input, so it is asked for each
# distinct code once. Passing the column as-is would put duplicate keys
# on both sides of the merge and multiply the rows.
records[[".postal_key"]] <- normalize_postal_code(records[[postal_col]])
postal_links <- resolve_postal(unique(records[[".postal_key"]]), all_links = TRUE)
joined <- merge(
  records, postal_links,
  by.x = ".postal_key", by.y = "postal_code",
  all.x = TRUE, sort = FALSE
)
joined[[".postal_key"]] <- NULL

dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
utils::write.csv(joined, file.path(output_dir, "postal_da.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
"
